inventive_nucleus: A slow-release chlorhexidine gluconate reservoir is integrated into the adhesive patch surrounding the glucose sensor insertion site to prevent infection.
mechanism: The slow-release CHG reservoir interacts with the adhesive patch to create a localized antimicrobial environment.
expected_effect: Reduced risk of glucose sensor insertion site infection.

predictions.observable: Glucose sensor insertion site infection rate
predictions.baseline: Current rate of 10% infection within 7 days of sensor insertion
predictions.expected_magnitude: 50% reduction within 30 days of sensor insertion
predictions.conditions: Use of Nucleus patch in 100 patients with diabetes for 30 days
predictions.falsifier: Failure to achieve a 40% reduction in infection rate within 30 days of sensor insertion in at least 80% of patients

falsification_tests: Failure to achieve a 40% reduction in infection rate within 30 days of sensor insertion in at least 80% of patients

experiment_plan.objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of a slow-release chlorhexidine gluconate reservoir in reducing glucose sensor insertion site infection rate
dependent_variables: Glucose sensor insertion site infection rate
controls: Use of standard adhesive patch without CHG reservoir
Standard glucose sensor insertion procedure without Nucleus patch
experiment_plan.baseline: Current rate of 10% infection within 7 days of sensor insertion
procedure: Recruit 100 patients with diabetes for the study
Randomly assign patients to either the Nucleus patch group or the control group
Insert glucose sensor in all patients using standard procedure
Monitor patients for 30 days and record infection rates
experiment_plan.expected_result: A 50% reduction in infection rate within 30 days of sensor insertion
experiment_plan.falsification_condition: Failure to achieve a 40% reduction in infection rate within 30 days of sensor insertion in at least 80% of patients
experiment_plan.safety_constraints: Ensure proper use and handling of Nucleus patch to prevent adverse reactions
experiment_plan.information_gain: Understanding the effectiveness of Nucleus patch in reducing glucose sensor insertion site infection rate, and potential for improved patient outcomes

commercial.economic_problem: Reduced healthcare costs due to lower infection rates and prolonged glucose sensor lifespan
commercial.likely_buyer: Healthcare providers, insurance companies, and pharmaceutical companies
commercial.manufacturing_relevance: High, as it involves integrating a slow-release reservoir into an adhesive patch, which requires specialized manufacturing processes
commercial.regulatory_path_hypothesis: FDA 510(k) clearance, as it is a medical device that improves the safety and efficacy of an existing device
commercial.commercial_classification: A|High commercial potential, as it addresses a significant problem in the medical technology industry and has a clear regulatory path
